newsitem.title: GERMANY: CalPERS declines comment on Deutsche Telekom IPO.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS declines comment on Deutsche Telekom IPO.

text.p: The head of the California Public Employees's Retirement System (CalPERS) on Monday declined comment on whether the pension fund, the largest in the U.S., would invest in Deutsche Telekom AG.
Telekom, the German telephone monopoly, is preparing to launch Europe's largest-ever initial public offering next month, expected to be worth some 15 billion marks.

"We'd look at all the (telecommunications) privatisations with some degree of interest," Jim Burton, chief executive of the $100 billion fund told Reuters in an interview when asked about the fund's interest in the Deutsche Telekom listing.
"We view telecommunications as a growth industry in every country in the future, particularly with the rapid development of technology," Burton said.
But Burton would not comment directly on Telekom's listing or on how he thought the company's share would perform.
Telekom plans an initial public offering beginning November 18 in Germany and New York. It will be the first stage in the privatisation of the state-owned telecommunications giant.
Full privatisation will not be completed until after the year 2000, when the German government is expected to give up its majority holding in the company.
In addition to listings in Germany and New York, Telekom has said it is considering listing shares on bourses in Canada and Tokyo.
Telekom will release a detailed time plan for the listing in a preliminary sales prospectus to be released on October 4.
